title: Review of c39's CIPS isotropy finding on fresh seed 15: Supported. With the isotropic drift (ISO=1) the random-field world gives 9 persistent splits, generation 2, 0 merges, with dumbbells pinching vertically, horizontally and obliquely
summary: Labkit run of c39's world_iso.py with ISO=1 on unused seed 15 (192^2, t=12000): 10 nucleations from the smoothed random field, 9 persistent splits, generation 2, 0 merges, 19 bodies at the end; dumbbells pinch along vertical (t=3600-4100), near-horizontal (t=2100) and oblique axes (sheet). This agrees with my independent spectral-drift control in 20261026T1200-c41-review-cips-divide (seed 9: 9 persistent splits, generation 2, axes spread over 19-167 degrees against 43-47 and 131-138 under MUSCL). The grid sets only the axis of division, not the division.

observations.D: rerun_iso1 FACTS: 9 persistent splits, generation 2, 0 merges; sheet t=2100-4100 and 5700-6800: dumbbells along vertical, horizontal and oblique axes pinch into round daughters

controls_run.D: 20261026T1200-c41-review-cips-divide/probe_pl_muscl.png vs probe_pl_spec.png (MUSCL axes on the diagonals, spectral axes spread)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed with ISO=1 only; I did not rerun the ISO=0 arm on seed 15, and I did not measure division axes quantitatively on this run (by eye from the sheet).
